name: market stall of scavenged goods: faded army-green tarp roof seen from above, crate counter with scrap parts, folded cloth and a rusty can
label: wasteland_ruins/stall-b

surfaces.part: crate counter top with goods area
scrap parts, folded cloth, rusty can

answer.evidence: The tarp roof fills rows 0-13 with diagonal seams. A light front-edge line at row 13 (L=130) is followed by dark eave shadow at rows 14-15, so it reads as a sloped roof plane seen from above (evidence c). Below it the stall front runs rows 16-31: posts, a counter with goods in rows 16-23, and a crate front with plank bands in rows 23-31. The counter shows its back area at rows 17-22. No receding side face is drawn, and the narrow brown strips at the left and right edges are posts.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 11 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it is in range with the hedge at 9 but below the closest same-kind references. Near-flat coverage is 6%, between the stall's 13% and the hedge's 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, which means the outline is tinted. It reads as dark green beside the tarp and dark brown beside the crates, not a black sticker line. The tarp roof has about 4 green steps with some fold and seam variation, and a highlight band. The crate counter below is more compressed: the crate face and the scrap, cloth and can items are small, with few steps and little grain. They look flatter than the cheese stall's goods and awning, which carry per-item shading and stripes. Overall it is clean and consistent but thinner in shading depth (about 4 steps against 5-6) and in texture than the best references. Because of that shortfall, I fail it.

The tarp has about 4 green steps (highlight edge, light, mid, dark) with some fold and stripe detail, but fewer than the 5-6 steps on the cheese-stall awning and well roof. The crate counter below is a large, dark, low-contrast block with few per-plank highlights or grain. The scrap parts, cloth and can are tiny and read as a few pixels each.
